FINDING_ID: MM_F001
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: In §7.4, the derivation claim “When this inequality holds, dY/dt > 0 despite declining finding rate” is mathematically incomplete as stated for the defined quantity \(Y(t)=N(t)\bar H(t)\). Differentiating gives
\[
\frac{dY}{dt}= \lambda(t)\bar H(t)+N(t)\frac{d\bar H}{dt},
\]
since \(dN/dt=\lambda(t)\). The appendix’s guard compares \((d\bar H/dt)/\bar H\) to \(|d\lambda/dt|/\lambda\), which is about the decay of the rate \(\lambda\), not the sign of \(dY/dt\). But \(dY/dt>0\) depends on \(\lambda\) and \(N\), not on \(d\lambda/dt\). In fact, if \(\lambda>0\) and \(\bar H\ge 0\), then \(dY/dt>0\) already holds whenever \(d\bar H/dt\ge -\lambda \bar H/N\); no comparison to \(d\lambda/dt\) is required. So the claimed inequality is not the formal condition for \(dY/dt>0\) for the defined \(Y\); it is at best a heuristic condition for “deepening while rate decays.”
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the claim with one of:
1. a correct derivative statement for the current definition,
\[
dY/dt>0 \iff \lambda(t)\bar H(t)+N(t)\,d\bar H/dt>0,
\]
or
2. redefine the relevant instantaneous quantity as \(y(t)=\lambda(t)\bar H(t)\), for which
\[
\frac{dy}{dt}>0 \iff \frac{1}{\bar H}\frac{d\bar H}{dt} > -\frac{1}{\lambda}\frac{d\lambda}{dt},
\]
matching the relative-rate inequality already written.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: The “Feedback into \(G_n\)” section claims: “Replace \(E_{\text{claimed}}\) with \(E^*(t)\) in the \(p_H\) calculation.” But the formal definition of \(p_{H,j,k}\) in §6 uses \(E\), not \(E_{\text{claimed}}\):
\[
p_{H,j,k}=\min\left(1, f_k(E,M)\prod_s(1+\lambda_sV_s)\right), \quad f_k(E,M)=E(\alpha+(1-\alpha)M).
\]
So the document switches symbols midstream between \(E\), \(E_{\text{claimed}}\), and \(E^*(t)\) without defining the relation. This is more than notation sloppiness: it creates an ambiguity about whether the initial \(E\) in the model is supposed to be self-reported expertise, latent true expertise, or current posterior estimate.
PROPOSED_FIX: Introduce explicit notation:
- \(E_{\text{claim}}\): self-declared expertise used before calibration,
- \(E^*(t)\): posterior calibrated estimate after \(t\) reviews,
- initial operational rule: use \(E=E_{\text{claim}}\) at \(t=0\), then replace with \(E=E^*(t)\) once sufficient data exists.
Update all equations and prose consistently.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: The Beta-Binomial update for HIL expertise in §6 is underspecified/internally inconsistent about what constitutes a “trial.” The posterior
\[
E^*(t)=\frac{a_0+\sum \text{catches}}{a_0+b_0+\sum \text{trials}}
\]
is standard only if each trial is a Bernoulli opportunity with a well-defined success/failure outcome. But the appendix never defines whether “trials” are findings reviewed, flaw opportunities, tasks, rounds, or claims. The accompanying table is indexed by “Reviews completed,” implying one denominator; the formula uses \(\sum \text{trials}\), implying potentially many Bernoulli events per review. Without a defined sampling unit, \(E^*(t)\) is not operationally well-defined, and the “approximately five reviews” claim is not mathematically anchored.
PROPOSED_FIX: Define the Bernoulli unit explicitly, e.g. “each independently verifiable flaw opportunity in class \(k\)” or “each reviewed claim with adjudicated ground truth.” If reviews aggregate multiple Bernoulli trials, rewrite the table label to “adjudicated opportunities completed,” not “reviews completed.” If each review is one trial, say so and justify the reduction.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 3
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: The appendix reuses \(F_n\) with incompatible meanings inside §6. Earlier and elsewhere, \(F_n\) denotes the total structured coverage scalar:
\[
F_n=\sum_k w_k\left[1-\prod_i(1-d_{ik}p_{ik})\right].
\]
But in §6, the reduction row “\(n_H=0 \to F_n\)” is only correct after aggregating over classes, while the line “\(C_M(k)\) — machine cumulative detection (= \(F_n\))” conflates the per-class quantity with the global weighted sum. Some prior findings caught one manifestation; the broader miss is that the section alternates between per-class and aggregate levels without a separate symbol for machine-only aggregate \(G_n^{(M)}\) or \(F_n^{(M)}\), which causes multiple downstream reduction statements to be ill-typed.
PROPOSED_FIX: Use distinct symbols:
- \(C_{M,k}\) for per-class machine coverage,
- \(F_n^{(M)}=\sum_k w_k C_{M,k}\) for aggregate machine-only coverage.
Then state reductions only at the correct level: \(n_H=0 \Rightarrow G_n=F_n^{(M)}\).
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: The asymmetric calibration metric
\[
\kappa_{\text{asym}}=1-\beta\max(0,E_{\text{claimed}}-E^*(t))-\max(0,E^*(t)-E_{\text{claimed}})
\]
is presented as a “calibration score,” but it is not bounded below by 0 and can become negative, as the table explicitly shows for the “bluffer.” That breaks the ordinary interpretation of a score or metric on a calibrated scale and makes comparisons inconsistent with the symmetric \(\kappa\in[0,1]\). It is not wrong to define an unbounded penalty-like quantity, but calling it the same kind of calibration score without domain specification is mathematically inconsistent with the prior score semantics.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either:
- specify the codomain explicitly as \((-\infty,1]\) and rename it to an asymmetric calibration penalty score, or
- clip it to \([0,1]\): \(\kappa_{\text{asym}}^{\text{clip}}=\max(0,\kappa_{\text{asym}})\).
Also update the interpretation text accordingly.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006
SEVERITY: 0.64
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59
DESCRIPTION: §8.2 defines the emergence threshold using “bootstrap standard error of the \(Y\) estimates”:
\[
Y_{\text{composite}}(t) > \max\{Y_i(t)\} + k\hat\sigma(Y).
\]
But \(\hat\sigma(Y)\) is a standard error, while \(k=1.96\) is invoked as if the distribution were normal and the target were a two-sided 95% confidence interval. For a bootstrap SE, \(1.96\hat\sigma\) is only a normal approximation, not a bootstrap confidence bound. More importantly, the statistic being compared is a max-vs-single composite contrast, so the uncertainty should be on the contrast \(Y_{\text{composite}}-\max_i Y_i\), not on “the Y estimates” generically. As written, the threshold is mathematically underdefined.
PROPOSED_FIX: Define the resampling target explicitly:
- bootstrap the contrast \(\Delta_Y = Y_{\text{composite}}-\max_i Y_i\),
- declare emergence if the lower 95% bootstrap percentile (or BCa) bound of \(\Delta_Y\) exceeds 0.
If retaining the SE shortcut, state it as a normal approximation and define exactly which estimator’s SE is used.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007
SEVERITY: 0.62
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: The appendix claims in §5 that \(G_n\) is “well-defined, all reductions verified,” but no implementation of \(G_n\), \(C_H(k)\), HIL priming correlation \(\rho_{MH}\), or the HIL calibration machinery exists in `dynamic_management.py`. This is a model-to-code discrepancy distinct from previously noted semantic drifts: the appendix’s implementation-status framing implies practical integrability, while the actual referenced orchestration artifact contains no code path for combined machine-HIL detection at all.
PROPOSED_FIX: In the appendix, change the status row for \(G_n\) from implementation-adjacent language to “specified only; not implemented in dynamic_management.py.” If intended to be implemented here, add explicit classes/functions for machine/HIL combined detection and calibration, or move the status reference to the file that actually implements it.
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: The notation summary lists \(G_n\) as “White paper §7.1, this appendix §6,” but the appendix body itself introduces §6 as the combined machine-HIL detection model and earlier prose refers to “white paper Part III” for review structure, not a prior canonical \(G_n\) definition. PROPOSED_FIX: If the white paper truly defines \(G_n\), quote that exact section and present §6 as refinement/extension. Otherwise change the notation row to “This appendix §6” only.
